messages.content: After a tab switch the orchestrator tokens still arrive, but sql_analyst and chart-builder chunks look like a second stream and the original thinking block disappears.
When switching back to the original conversation, keep the in-progress agent response and thinking process visible instead of losing it.
Orchestrator and subagent replies, including sql_analyst and chart-builder, must share one progressive handler attached to the owning conversation so in-progress tokens stay on that tab.
When switching back to the original conversation, keep the in-progress agent response and thinking process visible instead of losing it.
Reopening a question tab currently redraws free-text history, but the earlier interactive prompt with its option buttons is gone.
After switching back to the original question, show the ask_user_question block inside the thinking block and preserve its selectable options.
ask_user_question is first-class conversation state with selectable options, not just free text, and must be restored when a question tab is revisited.
After switching back to the original question, show the ask_user_question block inside the thinking block and preserve its selectable options.
A follow-up in the second browser tab showed the opening user message from the first tab, including its uploaded session file name.
Fix follow-up messages so each conversation returns its own first message instead of reading the first message from another conversation.
X-Session-ID is one per browser tab; each conversation may read only its own message history and session file and must not leak across conversations.
Fix follow-up messages so each conversation returns its own first message instead of reading the first message from another conversation.
Chart and text interleaving looks correct on Anthropic, but gpt5.2 through the gateway drops the structured example and retries as if the prompt were Anthropic-specific.
Make the chart-text-interleaving instruction work for OpenAI gpt5.2 as well as Anthropic models, without relying on Anthropic-only behavior.
Models route through Bifrost; system prompt structure, examples, retries, and chart/text interleaving must stay model-agnostic rather than Anthropic-only.
Make the chart-text-interleaving instruction work for OpenAI gpt5.2 as well as Anthropic models, without relying on Anthropic-only behavior.
Skill creation currently writes files in one shot after the first prompt, and users only see the result after it already exists.
Change Skill creation so the agent drafts a plan, asks the user to review and revise it until satisfied, and only then creates the Skill.
For Skill creation and other multi-step generation, plan first, use ask_user_question for explicit review, iterate on feedback, and execute only after approval.

Read e2e/test-results and fix all skills-related errors in the Playwright scenarios and runner code.
Map each e2e/test-results failure artifact to its scenario YAML and runner spec, fix the failing behavior, and rerun only the affected scenario without weakening assertions.

Update the README project structure to match the latest repository tree and current feature layout.

A fresh Linux clone starts compose, then Skill writes fail with permission denied on the bind-mounted skills directory; host chmod is the first workaround people try.
Fix the skills write permission denied error found when cloning and starting services on Linux, and verify the compose deployment.
Fix bind-mount ownership in the image with host UID/GID adaptation, use a crypto.randomUUID polyfill for insecure origins, and never host-side chmod; verify on a second fresh clone.
Fix the skills write permission denied error found when cloning and starting services on Linux, and verify the compose deployment.
Asking the agent which Skills it has still returns a simplified Skill. PreToolUse already blocks invocation, so listing remains; the wrong prompt file was edited last time.
Stop the agent from returning a simplified Skill when asked which Skills it has, and change the correct prompt surface without affecting unrelated tool behavior.

The sidecar may generate HTML for a data-plugin dashboard, but the current frontend has no path to display that generated HTML, so document the missing delivery path rather than adding a UI route in this change.
